notes: SHIP v1.14.398 - M1-b: COVERAGE IS MEASURED AGAINST LIVE STORAGE, NOT ASSERTED FROM A LIST. The .397 registry was verified on a live device immediately after shipping and it was INCOMPLETE. Three real keys were missing: deploy_forge_loadout_v1, deploy_forge_view_v1 and phantom_audits_v1 - the last of which is completed audits, and was named in the original storage audit. All three are added here. WHY THEY WERE MISSED, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE MISS. Every one of them is reached as a string literal passed into a wrapper - store.set('deploy_forge_loadout_v1', ...) or a function-local const KEY = 'phantom_audits_v1' - so NEITHER a key-constant grep NOR a localStorage.getItem/setItem grep can see them. The registry was built by reading the source, and reading the source cannot enumerate keys that are reached indirectly. That is the same failure mode as the hand-written export it replaced: correct until someone adds a key, and silent when they do. THE STRUCTURAL FIX. phantom_backupCoverage() enumerates what is ACTUALLY in localStorage at runtime and subtracts three explicit lists - keys carried by a named bundle section, keys in the registry, and keys deliberately excluded with a stated reason. Anything left over is a key nobody has classified. It is now reported three ways rather than dropped: a console warning, a toast at export time, and an unclassifiedKeys array recorded inside the bundle itself, so the gap is visible in the backup file and not only in a console the technician will never open. The two named/excluded lists were promoted from a comment into real arrays so the check has something to measure against. THE PRINCIPLE. A registry that can only be verified by reading code is not a safety mechanism, it is a promise. Measuring against live storage is the difference between believing coverage is complete and knowing which keys are unaccounted for. This is the same shape as the M0 lesson: the instrument that measures the thing has to be trustworthy before the thing it measures can be trusted. VERIFIED ON THE LIVE BUILD BEFORE THIS SHIP: registry round-trip is byte-identical for every captured key; of 12 keys present on the test device, 5 were uncovered and 4 of those were correct exclusions (session state, tab presence, brief timestamp, seen-boot flag) - the fifth was deploy_forge_loadout_v1, which is what triggered this ship. Also confirmed NOT keys, so deliberately not added: phantom_master_v2 (a comment about future schema), phantom_deployment_id (an IndexedDB index name), phantom_lead_ (sessionStorage, ephemeral by definition) and phantom_pin_salt_ (a hash salt string, not a storage key). GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, CSS braces 4557/4557, line endings preserved, 28 registry keys with no duplicates, three-stamp lockstep. STILL TO COME IN M1: safeGet and safeRemove, phantom_node_status_v1 through safeStore, the two unguarded BOM setItem calls, ge_load read-modify-write, the corrupt-data quarantine path, and precaching pdf.min.js. DEVICE-VERIFY: with a real deployment loaded, EXPORT FULL BACKUP. Expect NO unrecognised-key toast. Open the downloaded JSON and confirm it contains a keys object and that unclassifiedKeys is an empty array.
